articles.title: A Systematic Review of New, Enhanced Surveillance Systems and Methodologies for Zoonotic Influenza Viruses in Animals and Human-Animal Interface.

diseases.name_zh: 人感染高致病性禽流感

en.research_question: The authors aimed to evaluate recent developments in monitoring techniques for animal and cross-species influenza viruses to determine which innovations warrant broader application and which areas require further investigation.
en.study_design: This work follows a systematic review framework guided by PRISMA standards, synthesizing data from 164 selected publications out of an initial search yielding 7,490 records.
en.population_setting: The scope encompasses global efforts to track influenza strains circulating among wildlife, livestock, and humans, with particular attention to interaction zones where spillover events occur.
en.main_findings: The analysis identifies multiple technological improvements alongside persistent structural deficiencies in monitoring networks. Current documentation indicates that numerous regions operate without robust cross-sectoral tracking systems, resulting in incomplete estimates of infection prevalence. Priority actions emphasize integrating multi-sectoral datasets, standardizing new testing tools, scaling passive sampling strategies, and aligning technical upgrades with regulatory decision-making.
en.public_health_relevance: Strengthening coordinated monitoring frameworks is presented as essential for reducing seasonal illness impacts and mitigating future outbreak threats through improved diagnostic readiness and targeted research funding.
en.limitations: The evaluation relies exclusively on indexed academic publications, which may overlook operational field data or reflect uneven research investment across different geographic areas. Additionally, the focus on a seven-year window restricts historical context for long-term trend analysis.
en.gids_interpretation: This publication offers a consolidated perspective on methodological evolution within cross-species pathogen tracking initiatives. It contextualizes recent scholarly contributions toward standardized data collection and policy alignment without referencing active epidemiological dashboards or real-time transmission metrics.

articles.title: Resurgent threat in a changing climate: A 20-year bibliometric analysis of global Chikungunya research evolution and pandemic preparedness

en.research_question: Maps two decades of global scientific output to determine current priorities and unmet needs in chikungunya pandemic readiness.
en.study_design: Bibliometric evaluation of 8,125 indexed articles published between 2004 and 2025, utilizing software tools to track citation trends, author networks, and keyword co-occurrence patterns.
en.population_setting: Global scientific literature and publishing records rather than a defined clinical or demographic cohort.
en.main_findings: Article production expanded sevenfold following 2013, coinciding with major regional outbreaks. Research activity concentrated within four primary national hubs. Scholarly focus has progressively shifted toward immunization development and environmental transmission factors, while diagnostic differentiation and crisis management keywords have diminished in frequency.
en.public_health_relevance: Highlights increasing academic investment in vaccine platforms and climate-linked transmission models. Identifies structural imbalances in multinational research partnerships and recommends aligning pathogen readiness initiatives with broader environmental health planning.
en.limitations: Analysis depends entirely on database-indexed publications, potentially overlooking non-traditional or regionally restricted research outputs. The methodology quantifies scholarly productivity and thematic shifts rather than measuring actual disease incidence or intervention effectiveness.
en.gids_interpretation: Functions as a retrospective mapping of academic publishing trends instead of an active monitoring report. Offers context on how research emphasis has evolved toward preventive technologies and ecological drivers without generating new empirical signal data.

articles.title: Salmonellosis Outbreak in a Rottweiler Kennel Associated with Raw Meat-Based Diets

en.research_question: To characterize the clinical presentation, microbiological profile, and environmental spread of a Salmonella infection within a canine breeding facility.
en.study_design: A descriptive case report and outbreak investigation utilizing clinical observation, sample collection, and laboratory diagnostics.
en.population_setting: A Bulgarian Rottweiler breeding kennel comprising adult and post-partum dogs.
en.main_findings: Affected animals exhibited gastrointestinal symptoms and lethargy, with more severe presentations occurring in recently whelped females. Microbiological testing revealed extensive bacterial shedding among the dogs alongside contamination of their diet and surrounding surfaces. Full recovery followed the cessation of raw diet administration, implementation of targeted drug therapy, and thorough sanitation, while exposed humans remained uninfected.
en.public_health_relevance: The report highlights the cross-species transmission potential of pathogens found in unregulated raw animal feed. It advocates for enhanced feed traceability and biosecurity standards to mitigate health threats under a collaborative veterinary-human health approach.
en.limitations: The evaluation relies on observational data from a single facility without a comparative control cohort. Consequently, the observed outcomes may not reflect broader canine populations or different regional conditions.
en.gids_interpretation: This article contributes to the academic record of veterinary infectious disease events and diagnostic methodologies. Its documentation aids scholarly monitoring of dietary-related microbial risks in domestic animal settings.

zh.research_question: 本文探讨了一名完成四剂疫苗接种的青少年在突破感染蜱传脑炎后的临床表现、诊断标志物特征及长期预后。
zh.study_design: 该研究为单病例报告，详细记录了一名患者的临床病程、实验室检测数据及影像学随访结果。
zh.population_setting: 研究对象为一名既往健康的早期青少年，已完成四剂蜱传脑炎疫苗接种。
zh.main_findings: 尽管完成全程接种，患者仍发生重症突破感染并住院三个月。血清学显示典型IgM反应延迟，而脑脊液中针对非结构蛋白1的早期IgG应答具有较高诊断价值。初始治疗曾按自身免疫性脑炎进行免疫调节干预，多年随访的脑部影像学检查证实存在持续性病变，但导致严重预后的具体机制尚不明确。
zh.public_health_relevance: 该案例提示在已接种疫苗人群中仍需警惕突破感染的可能，并强调了特定生物标志物在鉴别诊断中的潜在作用，对完善相关疾病的临床识别策略具有参考价值。

zh.gids_interpretation: 该文献属于个案报道范畴，主要提供特定人群下罕见突破感染的临床细节与实验室特征，有助于丰富现有疾病认知框架，但不涉及实时监测数据的关联分析。

en.research_question: How can clinicians characterize the clinical trajectory and laboratory markers associated with a rare post-vaccination neurological complication?
en.study_design: This investigation utilizes a descriptive case report format to document a single patient encounter.
en.population_setting: The subject is a previously healthy adolescent who had received four prior vaccinations against the targeted pathogen.
en.main_findings: The individual developed severe encephalitis requiring extended hospitalization despite complete immunization history. Laboratory analysis indicated a postponed IgM reaction but demonstrated early IgG production targeting the NS1 protein within cerebrospinal fluid. Longitudinal imaging confirmed enduring neurological alterations, while the precise drivers of the severe progression were not determined.
en.public_health_relevance: The documentation emphasizes the continued possibility of serious neurological illness in fully immunized populations. It also suggests that medical professionals should maintain awareness of infectious triggers when evaluating acute inflammatory symptoms.
en.limitations: The singular focus on one patient prevents generalization to wider demographic groups or definitive mechanistic conclusions. Authors explicitly acknowledge that the factors contributing to the severe clinical course remain unknown.
en.gids_interpretation: This record offers background context on atypical immunological profiles and diagnostic methodologies following prophylactic administration. It functions as a reference resource for understanding complex clinical presentations without implying active monitoring activity.

articles.title: Tick-borne encephalitis in the Åland Islands, Finland: incidence and disease course since the implementation of a general TBE vaccination programme.

related_surveillance.method: high-confidence article geography intersected with GIDS series coverage

en.research_question: What are the epidemiological trends, clinical characteristics, and long-term prognoses of tick-borne encephalitis in an endemic Finnish archipelago after routine immunization began?
en.study_design: A retrospective observational analysis examining medical records and laboratory results for confirmed cases spanning nearly two decades.
en.population_setting: Individuals diagnosed with the viral infection in the Åland Islands, Finland, between 2006 and 2023 using standardized European diagnostic standards.
en.main_findings: The analysis identified 145 cases with a median annual incidence of twenty-nine per one hundred thousand residents. Hospitalization was common, disease severity increased with patient age, and two deaths occurred. Most survivors regained clinical function within two years, though partial vaccination histories showed higher rates of breakthrough illness.
en.public_health_relevance: Stable regional case counts contrast with rising trends elsewhere, suggesting potential benefits from sustained immunization efforts. Monitoring disease patterns across different vaccination statuses may help guide future preventive planning.
en.limitations: The retrospective chart review design inherently limits causal inference and introduces potential documentation biases. The absence of a concurrent comparison group restricts the ability to isolate intervention effects from other epidemiological factors.
en.gids_interpretation: This article documents longitudinal clinical and epidemiological observations for a specific arbovirus within a defined geographic area. The reported incidence figures and recovery rates offer contextual reference points for understanding regional disease dynamics.

articles.title: Transcriptomic signatures for diagnosing tuberculosis in clinical practice: a prospective, multicentre cohort study

en.research_question: Assess whether blood-based gene expression profiles can accurately identify tuberculosis among individuals presenting with clinically suspected disease in everyday medical practice.
en.study_design: A prospective, multicentre cohort investigation conducted across ten secondary care facilities in England.
en.population_setting: Individuals aged sixteen years and older seeking inpatient or outpatient care for suspected tuberculosis within a low-incidence national health system.
en.main_findings: Analysis of six hundred twenty-eight participants revealed that the top-performing novel molecular profile achieved an area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve of zero point eight seven, alongside seventy-seven percent sensitivity and eighty-four percent specificity for active infection. The strongest previously reported profile demonstrated similar metrics, yet neither category fulfilled World Health Organization benchmarks for paired sensitivity and specificity required by non-sputum assays. Diagnostic performance remained inadequate even when focusing exclusively on cases classified as highly probable tuberculosis.
en.public_health_relevance: Molecular blood testing represents an evolving diagnostic avenue that warrants continued methodological refinement before widespread implementation in routine infectious disease management.
en.limitations: Final disease classification relied on retrospective application of predefined criteria following a six-to-twelve-month observation period rather than immediate confirmatory testing. Enrollment was confined to a single nation with established hospital networks, which may constrain broader applicability.
en.gids_interpretation: This record documents baseline performance metrics for transcriptomic diagnostic tools within a structured observational framework. The information establishes reference points for technical validation efforts without suggesting alignment with ongoing epidemiological tracking initiatives.

zh.research_question: 评估血液转录组特征在常规临床实践中对疑似结核病患者的诊断准确性。
zh.study_design: 本研究为嵌套于大型验证项目中的前瞻性多中心队列研究，在英国十家二级医疗机构同步开展。
zh.population_setting: 纳入对象为十六岁及以上、在常规门诊或住院环境中因临床表现怀疑感染结核病的成年患者。
zh.main_findings: 在六百二十八名完成分析的患者中，表现最优的新型与既往发表的特征集曲线下面积分别达到零点八七与零点八三。尽管各项指标显示一定区分能力，但所有测试模型均未达到世界卫生组织规定的非痰液检测敏感性特异性配对目标。
zh.public_health_relevance: 现有基于全血基因表达谱的分子工具在当前低流行地区的常规诊疗流程中可能缺乏足够的临床应用价值。
zh.limitations: 研究样本仅来源于低发病率国家的特定医疗体系，且最终确诊需依赖长达数月的后续追踪与预设标准，这可能限制结论向其他流行病学背景的推广。
zh.gids_interpretation: 该文献记录了前瞻性队列中分子标志物的实际诊断效能数据，可为相关技术的可发现性与临床转化背景提供信息参考，不涉及任何实时监测信号的推断。
